objectives: I can understand a spoken conversation about someone's day in Simple Past.
I can describe my own yesterday to a partner using at least 3 Simple Past sentences.
I can use key irregular Simple Past forms correctly (went, had, got, ate, took, was).

stages.name: Opening — retrieval and bridge
stages.purpose: Recall Simple Past forms and Mia's diary from lesson 1 before moving to new listening and speaking work.

procedure.text: Quick fire (whole class, oral): call out base verbs — go, eat, do, have, get, take. Pupils call back Simple Past form. Accept any correct attempt.
Mia recall (oral, 3 questions): 'What did Mia eat for breakfast?' / 'How did she get to school?' / 'What did she do after school?' Pupils answer in chorus or hands up.
Think-write: 'Write one Simple Past sentence about Mia.' Pupils write in exercise books.
Two or three pupils share. Teacher corrects any verb form errors on the board.

Bridge (spoken): 'Last lesson you read Mia’s diary. Today you listen to a conversation between two real people, then you describe your own yesterday to a partner — no text to read from.' Write the two I-can statements on the board.

stages.name: Grammar recap — Simple Past
stages.purpose: Briefly revisit the Simple Past rule and key irregular forms before pupils meet them in extended listening input.

procedure.text: Display the grammar recap sheet. Point to the rule: regular (-ed) and the six irregular forms. Address any verb error noted in Stage 1.
Highlight the German contrast: 'In German: Ich habe gegessen — two words. In English: I ate — one word, no have.' Read two sentences from the dialogue they are about to hear.
Pupils write the six irregular forms in their vocab column: went, had, did, ate, saw, was/were. 30 seconds.

stages.name: Listening — Tom and Lisa’s Tuesday
stages.purpose: Build understanding of spoken Simple Past in context using two structured listen runs and a comprehension grid.

procedure.text: Set the scene: 'Two friends, Tom and Lisa, talk about their Tuesday. Draw a quick grid: four rows (Morning / Lunchtime / After school / Evening), two columns (Tom / Lisa).'
Listen run 1 (gist): teacher reads the dialogue at natural pace. Pupils listen only. After: ask 'Who had a busier afternoon — Tom or Lisa?'
Pupils write their gist answer (one word) in their book.
Listen run 2 (detail): teacher reads again, more slowly, pausing at each new time section. Pupils fill the grid with short notes.
Pupils complete the grid. Short notes only — not full sentences.

Partner compare grids. Class reveal: teacher reads answers aloud (Morning: Tom got up late, had milk, took bus / Lisa woke 6:30, had toast + banana, walked. Lunchtime: Tom went home, had soup / Lisa had sandwich in canteen. After school: Tom did homework, watched TV / Lisa went to football. Evening: Tom bed 9:30, tired / Lisa read, bed 9). Pupils self-correct in different colour.

stages.name: Speaking — pair dialogue, frame-fade
stages.purpose: Move from receptive understanding to genuine oral production of Simple Past using sentence frames faded after the first round.

procedure.text: Write frames on board: 'What did you do yesterday?' / 'I woke up at...' / 'Then I...' / 'After that I...' / 'Finally I...' / 'In the evening I...'. Model one full exchange with a volunteer.
Round 1 (frames visible): Partner A asks 'What did you do yesterday?' Partner B answers using at least 3 frames. Then swap. Both partners speak.
Erase all frames from the board. 'Now try without the frames — you remember the structure.'
Round 2 (no frames): same dialogue, new partner if possible. Teacher circulates and notes the top 2 errors.
Write the top 2 errors on board as full sentences. Class identifies and fixes them together.

stages.name: Wrap-up — self-assess and exit ticket
stages.purpose: Return to learning intentions for self-assessment and collect a brief written sample as a formative check.

procedure.text: Point to I-can statements on board. Pupils rate: thumbs up (confident), sideways (mostly), down (need more). Note rough split.
Exit ticket: 'Write 2 Simple Past sentences about YOUR yesterday. You have 3 minutes.'
Pupils hand in books open at exit ticket, or teacher photographs pages. Not graded — formative only.
Homework: 'Write 5 sentences about your yesterday — see the homework sheet.' Hand out or direct to class page.
Preview: 'Next lesson: Simple Past word order with time expressions and more speaking practice.'
Early finishers: MCQ comprehension or gap-fill on the class page.

differentiationNotes: Weaker pupils: keep board frames visible during Round 2 of speaking; allow 1 sentence for exit ticket; use MCQ (not gap-fill) as early-finisher task. Stronger pupils: in Round 2, partner asks follow-up questions (Why? / Who with? / How long?); exit ticket requires 3 sentences with at least one time expression; attempt error-correction worksheet.
